candidates.summary: isCrossingCurParam tests only IsCrossing(), not that the resolved name is the first parameter, so a named result `cur` in a crossing function with an unnamed first realm param is refused as the parameter
candidates.failure_scenario: `func namedResult(_ realm) (cur realm) { cur = nil; return cur }` in a realm package. The unnamed first parameter becomes `.arg_0` (preprocess.go:560), which the FuncTypeExpr naming rule allows (preprocess.go:2827), and IsCrossing() compares only Params[0].Type to gRealmType (types.go:1393), so the named result resolves to a crossing FuncDecl and the write is refused at preprocess with "cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter". The ADR's Decision ("Package-level vars, named results, and block-scoped shadows stay writable"), isCrossingCurParam's own godoc, and the new fixture zrealm_cur_other_legal.gno all state the opposite; the fixture only covers a non-crossing enclosing function (`func namedResult(x int) (cur realm)`), so the class the PR sweeps has a member it missed. Pre-existing: the base refuses it too via the name+type rule, so the loss is that the advertised fix does not reach this shape, not a regression.

Then add `&& ft.Params[0].Name == "cur"` to both arms and re-run, with go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_cur_.*\.gno$' to confirm no fixture regresses.
candidates.evidence: At 6d88deba7: `--- FAIL: TestFiles/zrealm_b2claims_namedresult.gno` / `unexpected panic: gno.land/r/demo/curnamedres/zrealm_b2claims_namedresult.gno:27:2-11: cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter: it names the realm this frame is executing as, and that binding is fixed for the life of the frame`. Identical panic at merge base b7845fb2d, so pre-existing, not caused by the diff. With `ft.IsCrossing() && ft.Params[0].Name == "cur"` in both switch arms: `ok github.com/gnolang/gno/gnovm/pkg/gnolang 0.050s` for the fixture and `ok ... 0.930s` for all 31 zrealm_cur_* filetests.

candidates.summary: the cur-call provenance check accepts a named result `cur` of a crossing function as a frame identity, so the ADR's "backstop with no known reachable source route" has one and it reports the wrong mistake
candidates.failure_scenario: `func forward(_ realm) (cur realm) { target(cur); return }` where `func target(cur realm)`. The provenance switch tests only `dft.IsCrossing()` on the declaring FuncDecl, so the named result passes as if it were the parameter; preprocess accepts, and installInheritedCur's identity check panics at runtime with "the value passed is not the caller's own cur (a stale capture from another frame, a sibling frame, or a rebound cur)", which names none of what the author wrote. The ADR's Consequences claim "The identity check is now a backstop with no known reachable source route"; this is plain source and reaches it. Fail-closed and pre-existing (same panic at the merge base), so the loss is a compile-time refusal turned into a misleading runtime abort.

Adding `|| dft.Params[0].Name != "cur"` to both arms at 2160 and 2169 moves it to preprocess.
